title: Trustworthy Artificial Intelligence for Autonomous Wheelchairs
summary: SUPSI and IDSIA built a laboratory demonstrator of the REXASI-PRO autonomous-wheelchair safety system; no source reports a result for wheelchair users.
source_collection: ITU AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025)
account: In a preprint of 13 March 2024, the SUPSI team reported that combining several sensors can improve the accuracy of road-crossing decisions by an autonomous wheelchair in a laboratory test. By June 2025 SUPSI and IDSIA had developed a laboratory demonstrator and a dataset of outdoor scenarios such as road crossing. The REXASI-PRO project closed on 30 September 2025. In its final report on CORDIS, the consortium states that test campaigns ran in Madrid and Genoa and that final tests involved 52 outside participants. The report gives no result for wheelchair users. Safer and more independent mobility for people with reduced mobility remains an intended benefit.
purpose: Support safe door-to-door mobility for people with movement or sensory impairments.

data.answer:
SUPSI and IDSIA developed a laboratory demonstrator for autonomous wheelchair safety. Independent mobility benefits remain prospective.

Road-crossing experiments with robots and simulated disturbances do not establish safe door-to-door travel by wheelchair users. The entry supplies no user mobility, injury, or quality-of-life outcome. A final demonstration planned for fall 2025 is not confirmed as completed by this June 2025 publication.

The project account does not separately evaluate AI’s contribution to the benefit.
